about.backgroundText: A BSc in Computer Science from Durham University (UK), then years inside enterprise-grade engineering. I care about the business case as much as the code, so technical decisions get made for the right reasons and delivered to production standard.
about.expertiseText: I work across the stack and across languages, choosing technology for what it does for the business, never for its own sake. That means fewer moving parts, lower running costs and systems your team can own after I leave.
about.photoAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki seated at a boardroom table beside floor-to-ceiling windows, a closed laptop and notebook in front of him
about.title: Trusted with systems that cannot fail.
about.description: At IBM, I work on Financial Transaction Manager, a payments platform for banks, where reliability and precision are non-negotiable. That is the standard every client engagement gets.
about.quote: Reliability isn’t a property of the software. It’s how the work gets done.
about.directBody: No account managers and no handover to juniors. The person who scopes the work is the person accountable for it.
about.scopeBody: Before work starts, you know the result we are aiming for, what will be delivered, by when, and who owns what.
about.riskBody: If a risk appears, you hear about it from me first, with a recommendation attached.

philosophy.photoAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki holding a marker beside a whiteboard covered in a hand-drawn system diagram
philosophy.label: The work
philosophy.title: Complexity is expensive. Clarity compounds.
philosophy.messTitle: Most growing companies end up here.
philosophy.messBody: Systems nobody dares to touch. Integrations held together by habit. AI bolted on wherever it would fit. Every release slower and riskier than the last, and no one able to say exactly why.
philosophy.clearBody: One architecture, with clear boundaries and clear ownership, and nothing in it that hasn’t earned its place. Your team moves faster, costs become predictable, and every next decision gets easier instead of harder.
philosophy.signoff: Getting from the first picture to the second is the work.
philosophy.diagramTitle: An architecture diagram that starts as a tangle of direct calls into one shared database, with seven open findings, and resolves into clean layers: clients, edge, domains that each own their data, an event bus, downstream consumers and a shared platform, with no open findings.

offer.label: How it works
offer.title: It starts with a straight answer.
offer.auditTitle: Technical audit or AI readiness assessment
offer.auditBody: A fixed-price review of your systems or your AI opportunity. You get a written verdict: what is costing you money, what to fix first and what it should return. It is yours to keep, whether or not we continue.
offer.buildBody: The priorities from the audit, built and shipped: automations, integrations or re-architecture. Scoped to a business result and priced on its value, not on hours.
offer.retainBody: A senior technical voice without a full-time executive hire. Roadmap, reviews, vendor and hiring decisions, and one person accountable for all of it.
offer.filter: This is not hourly development or staff augmentation, and I don’t compete on price. If the problem is worth solving properly, let’s talk.

person.label: About
person.title: I’ve built what I advise on.
person.story1: I studied Computer Science at Durham University in the UK, and today I work at IBM on the Financial Transaction Manager, software that banks rely on to process payments.
person.story2: Alongside that, I design and build complete products myself: the architecture, the data, the infrastructure, the interface, and now the AI inside them. So the person advising you is the person who can build it, with no sales team and no junior behind the curtain.
person.story3: Everyone wants software that works. I want hard problems, clear ownership and people who care about the quality under the hood as much as I do. If that sounds like your company, we should talk.
person.portraitAlt: Piotr J. Borowiecki standing in a navy suit, one hand in his pocket, against a dark studio backdrop
person.proofTitle: You don’t have to take my word for it.
person.ibmBody: Software engineer on Financial Transaction Manager, payment software used by banks.
person.nhsBody: University project, built alongside their developers.
person.liveBody: A product I designed and built, live today, with 430+ stars on GitHub.
person.storyLead: I’m Piotr, and I take software systems from the first architecture decision to production.
person.closingLead: I’m selective about what I take on.
person.storyPassion: Technology is also my passion. Nearly all of my time goes into building, at work or on my own projects, and most of what’s left goes into reading.
person.storyFocus: I specialise in e-commerce and fintech: checkouts, payments, stock and ledgers, the places where a bug has a price tag. My favourite projects are the complex, high-stakes ones, with real money moving through them and no room for guesswork.
person.storyStack: My favourite stack is TypeScript, React and TanStack Start or Next.js on the front, Go and Node.js behind them, PostgreSQL with Drizzle underneath, all of it running on Cloudflare.
person.storyTeach: I also teach. On <react>ReactProjects.com</react> and <angular>AngularProjects.com</angular>, platforms I built and run myself, developers learn to build advanced, complex projects from scratch, step by step, following industry best practices.
person.teachBody: Platforms I built and run, teaching advanced projects step by step.

ai.label: AI in production
ai.title: Output is cheap now. Judgment isn’t.
ai.intro: I work with AI every day, and I’ve seen first-hand how the best teams in the world run it. What separates them isn’t the model. It’s what surrounds it.
ai.messTitle: Without it, you get slop at speed.
ai.messBody: Code that looks right and isn’t. Agents that drift. A codebase nobody can untangle a year from now, produced faster than anyone can review it.
ai.guardrailsBody: What AI may touch, what it may never touch, and what happens when it’s wrong. Set before the first line is written.
ai.harnessBody: Tests, evaluations and review loops that prove the output instead of trusting it. Nothing counts until it passes.
ai.judgmentBody: Telling good from merely plausible takes years of building real systems. It’s the one part you can’t prompt, and the part you’re paying for.
ai.diagramTitle: A bundle of tangled strands labelled AI output passes through three gates, guardrails, harness and judgment. Most strands stop at a gate, and a few clean parallel lines reach production.
ai.closing: The return is measured in what you ship and what you never have to rebuild. An audit shows you where you stand.

pricing.label: How I price
pricing.title: I price outcomes, not hours.
pricing.lead: I don’t charge by the hour. You get a fixed price for an agreed result, set by what that result is worth to your business.
pricing.valueBody: We start with what the result is worth to you: revenue gained, cost removed, risk avoided. The price is set against that, not against how long the work takes.
pricing.fixedBody: A defined outcome and a fixed price, with options at different levels of scope, before any work begins. No timesheets, no meter running, no surprise invoices.
pricing.alignedBody: An hourly rate rewards slow work and penalises experience. A fixed price for a result means we want the same thing: the problem solved, properly and soon.
pricing.closing: Diagnosis comes first, and it’s paid work. I don’t write free proposals and I don’t compete in pitches.
